look_here_first: First look at the plant base and leaf tips. Wright's skullcap is a low bushy perennial with many stems from a persistent base and small entire leaves with rounded/obtuse tips. Its hairs are minute and the calyx can look nearly smooth to the naked eye. Then confirm the larger upward-curving blue-violet corolla and visorlike skullcap calyx.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: perennial herb, taprooted, several-many-stemmed at the base, usually 10–20 cm tall

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: stems four-sided, densely puberulent with minute sessile glandular hairs

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: leaves opposite and decussate, short-petiolate, ovate to elliptic

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: leaf margins entire and tips rounded/obtuse

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: leafy raceme with paired axillary flowers, often oriented mainly to one side

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: calyx two-lipped with a projecting visorlike scutellum; puberulent but often smoother-looking than S. drummondii

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: corolla mostly 13–18 mm long, with a cylindric tube that curves upward and a violet throat

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: fruit produces four small minutely warty nutlets

lookalikes.differences: Scutellaria drummondii: S. drummondii is an annual with acute-tipped leaves, more conspicuous glandular hairs, shorter pedicels (about 1–1.2 mm) and smaller corollas (about 5.5–10 mm). S. wrightii is perennial/bushy, round-tipped and larger-flowered. Scutellaria ovata: S. ovata is much taller and rhizomatous, with large triangular-ovate leaves having truncate/subcordate bases and crenate margins; its corolla is about 21–25 mm.
